My grill/smoker is in dire need of a deep clean. Its a charcoal only one, and the lip that the grates sit on has this black grease that builds up. I usually use warm water and an old rag, but it doesn't get completely clean that way.

What do y'all use to clean your grills?
just a grill brush and a hot fire, anything else is going to get messy quick.

Heat it up for for 15 min on fresh charcoal and brush it with a good brush, like Slyguy42o said. That's really all you need. If you really want it to shine, wipe it down with some paper towel dipped in canola or peanut oil after you brush it.
What about the interior that isn't part of the grates? That's where I see the black grease, usually along the edges of that protrude to hold up the grates.

To be honest I don't clean any part of my grills/ smokers other then the rack the food goes on. There are products that help dissolve grease like this one but I usually just fire up the grill or smoker really hot for 15 minutes and then wire brush the grills/racks and ignore the rest.

You should use a solvent in your warm water to help remove grease if you choose the more thorough clean, even dish washing soap is better then straight water.

For a few years that's all I've done as well, just get the coals fired up and let them bake the grates for 10 or so minutes. A good wire brush to clear them of any debris then a little canola oil brushed on before I do any grilling. I''ve wondered if I was using too much oil over time, and that's where the black grease is coming from.

Thanks for the tips though, I'll be sure to use them.
